Original proposal wording: The proposed moving Median + MAD threshold will achieve a higher average F1-score than at least one fixed-threshold baseline.
Observed evidence: Proposed macro F1 was 0.0966 across 10 configured files versus 0.0905 fixed percentile and 0.0925 fixed mean+k-sigma. On the 4 files with positive test labels, means were 0.2414 proposed, 0.2264 fixed percentile, and 0.2312 fixed mean+k-sigma.
Denominator: 4/10 test-positive files; 90 fits; file-level averages across W and seeds
Statistical evidence: Proposed vs fixed percentile: Wilcoxon p=0.625, Holm p=1.000; vs fixed mean+k-sigma: p=1.000, Holm p=1.000. Confidence intervals cross zero.
Decision: Directional evidence only; not statistically established. Small test-positive sample limits confidence.

Original proposal wording: The proposed method will reduce false-positive rates on some time series with changing normal variability.
Observed evidence: Among 8 files with usable high-variance normal points, proposed mean high-variance FPR=0.3989 versus 0.2021 fixed percentile, 0.2580 fixed mean+k-sigma, and 0.0778 rolling mean+3-sigma. Proposed FPR was lower in 2/8 files versus percentile and 3/8 versus fixed mean+k-sigma, but in 0/8 versus rolling mean+3-sigma.
Statistical evidence: Proposed vs rolling 3-sigma: paired t-test p=0.000983, Holm p=0.002950; direction is significantly worse. Comparisons vs fixed percentile and fixed mean+k-sigma were not significant.
Decision: Mixed at file level: some isolated improvements versus the two fixed thresholds, but clear average deterioration versus the rolling baseline. Do not claim general FPR reduction.

Original proposal wording: The proposed method will maintain or improve NAB score by detecting anomalies with fewer false alerts or earlier detection.
Observed evidence: Proposed event recall=1.000 and mean normalized delay fraction=0.1978, better than the comparison methods; however proposed FPR=0.2348 versus 0.0424-0.0893 and mean NAB-style test score=-2027.22 versus -270.56, -326.14, and -330.63.
Statistical evidence: NAB-style paired tests are low-powered at n=4; proposed vs rolling p=0.125, Holm p=0.375. The absolute mean score is markedly worse.
Decision: Not supported overall: earlier detections and higher event recall are outweighed by false alarms and much worse NAB-style score.
